question.:question/problem:
![](images/8e/8eb53506d9e01d09fe3e072a2c6ed1ade05e1cc185693bdd66b34bdf75797ad9.png)

Which of the following statements are true with respect to the function $y=f(x)$ whose graph is plotted above.

Select all that apply.

- **I.** ${lim}_{x\to \,{2}^{-}}f(x)$ is finite
- **II.** ${lim}_{x\to \,{2}^{+}}f(x)$ is finite
- **III.** $f(x)$  has a discontinuity at $x=2$
question.:question/worked-solution:
By inspecting the graph, we can conclude the following:

- Statement I is false. We get ${lim}_{x\to \,{2}^{-}}f(x)=-\infty .$

- Statement II is true. We get ${lim}_{x\to \,{2}^{+}}f(x)=3.$

- Statement III is true. The function contains a break exactly at $x=2$ and it's impossible to draw its graph without taking our pencil off of the paper.

question.:question/problem:
![](images/51/5143df65d0f99c6511dc8ab13262831669c88535e19c986dacdb364e04847f58.png)

Which of the following statements are true with respect to the function $y=f(x)$ whose graph is plotted above.

Select all that apply.

- **I.** $f(x)$ is defined at $x=2$
- **II.** ${lim}_{x\to \,2}f(x)\ne f(2)$
- **III.** $f(x)$ has a discontinuity at $x=2$
question.:question/worked-solution:
By inspecting the graph, we can conclude the following:

- Statement I is true. We have $f(2)=2.$

- Statement II is false. Indeed, from the graph we see that

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to \,{2}^{-}}f(x) & =2, \\ {lim}_{x\to \,{2}^{+}}f(x) & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, ${lim}_{x\to \,2}f(x)=2=f(2).$

- Statement III is false. The graph of the function doesn't have a break at $x=2$ and we can draw the graph of $f(x)$ around $x=2$ without taking our pencil off of the paper.

- Statement III is false. The function contains a break exactly at $x=-1$ and it's impossible to draw its graph without taking our pencil off of the paper.

${lim}_{x\to \,1}f(x)=1.$

- Statement III is false. The function is not even defined at $x=1.$ The graph contains a break at $x=1.$ It's impossible to draw the graph of $f(x)$ without taking our pencil off of the paper.
